label: Original-phase position >= 3 (4th input token onward, before <DEL>)
explanation: Fires on every original-phase input step from t=3 to L-1 (dev precision 1.0, recall 0.965, mass recall 0.995), whatever the token identity. It never fires at t=0-1, on the <DEL> step (17 negligible activations), or anywhere in the copy phase. The only misses are weak activations (~0.09 of max) at t=2 in about 13% of sequences. Magnitude depends on position: about 0.55 of max at t=3, rising to about 0.8-1.0 by t=5-6, and often falling slightly over the last original tokens of long sequences. Token identity, digits and repeats barely change it (in_first lift reflects position, since later steps are more often repeats).

issues: Every claim I checked holds up. On the test split, (phase==0)&(t>=3) gets precision 1.0 with 0 false positives, recall 0.964, F1 0.982 and mass recall 0.995.

The only misses are 63,785 steps, all at t=2, about 0.09-0.11 of max, holding 0.5% of the activation mass. They are not explained by length: t==2 fires at about the same rate for L==3 (precision 0.133) as for L>=4 (precision 0.127). The examples include both repeated and non-repeated tokens, so they look like a weak partial onset of the feature, not a separate class.

On the copy phase, it is active on only 18 of 500k phase==1 steps (precision 3.6e-5). The dev profile shows exactly 0 copy-phase activations, and 17 on the <DEL> step, so 'never fires in the copy phase' is essentially correct.
Widening to t>=2 drops F1 to 0.89 (precision 0.80), so starting at t>=3 is the right cutoff.

Minor caveat: I did not score the magnitude-by-position description (about 0.55 at t=3 rising to about 0.8-1.0) directly. The t=2 miss examples are consistent with it: the following t=3 step sits around 0.52-0.60 and later steps around 0.75-0.85.
